text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan proposes disarmament of Cyprus and the Aegean. A decision is expected on banning overflights on Friday during a meeting between President Glafcos Clerides and Greek Premier Costas Simitis.
- The government will not back down on purchase of S-300 missile system.
- Cyprus did not bow to US on missile purchase, says Clerides.
- Clerides and United Nations play down US envoy's optimism on a military dialogue.
- Clerides and Simitis will discuss a temporary ban on military overflights in Cyprus on Friday.
- The government comes under pressure to accept the highest bid for the construction of the Limassol-Paphos road.
- Nicosia and the United Nations dismiss US claims of an agreement on the military dialogue.
- Russia wants to tax Russian offshore companies based in Cyprus.
- Taps turn off today in Nicosia as stringent water cuts come into effect.
- Two companies sue the state-run electricity authority seeking cancellation of tender for supply of generators.
